inline.s: [Eryang] a Sanskrit transliteration, also written Eryan. A free rendering is

the realm of wisdom. The Treasury of the Śrīmālā Sutra (Shengman Baoku) says: “Eryan is called the mother of wisdom, for wisdom is born from it, and so it is also named the realm of wisdom.” [Shengman Baoku] is also written
Treasury of the Śrīmālā Sutra
. Composed by Jizang of the Sui dynasty (549-623
years
), it is
the
most exhaustive commentary on the Śrīmālā Sutra.
“All things are without nirvāṇa, there is no Buddha that attains nirvāṇa, and no nirvāṇa that a Buddha attains.”
Nirvāṇa
is likewise an affair within a dream
there is
no nirvāṇa
of the
Buddhas,
there are
no
Buddhas
that
enter
nirvāṇa.
[No nirvāṇa for all things]
this is an inverted construction, used to heighten the emphasis. Its meaning is: there is no nirvāṇa for anything at all.
The World-Honored One understood deeply that the ten dharma-realms are but a dream of ignorance, and so nirvāṇa and the Buddha
too
are all illusions; there is no real nirvāṇa, no real Buddha who enters nirvāṇa, and no real event of a Buddha entering nirvāṇa
at all
. In the Perfect Enlightenment Sutra the Buddha says:
“Samsara and nirvāṇa, ordinary beings and all Buddhas, are alike the aspect of flowers in the sky.”
“Far from awareness
and the object of awareness, whether there is or whether there is not, both of these are wholly abandoned.”
The World-Honored One
is far from awareness and its object,
regardless of
whether dharmas exist
or
do not
exist,
these
two are both far removed.
“The Muni, in still contemplation, is thus far from arising; this is called non-grasping, and pure in the present world and the world beyond.”
Reverently
following
the World-Honored One’s
still contemplation,
he is
far from all
illusory forms
such a wondrous dharma
is named non-grasping; pure in the present world and the world beyond
forever
pure.
[Still contemplation] all dharmas are originally still
, without arising or ceasing
. The Avataṃsaka Sutra says:
“Contemplating the still dharma, one extinguishes all stupidity and darkness.”
The Perfect Enlightenment Sutra says:

“To know illusion is already to leave it, no further expedient is needed; to leave illusion is already to awaken, and there is no gradation either.” Hence the patriarchs say: “When the wild mind does not rest, this very rest is bodhi.”

Above, Mahāmati’s verse of praise to the Buddha says: “Whether there is or whether there is not, both of these are wholly abandoned.” This is the non-dual dharma-gate, wherein existence and non-existence are both abandoned.
The abandonment of both existence and non-existence is the essential purport of this sutra.

Because what Mahāmati asks below are all dharmas of existence and non-existence (all names, marks, and false imagining), the World-Honored One therefore answers: all of these are negated. This is to cause one to abandon them and let go of them. If one can fully abandon them and let go, that is self-realized noble wisdom.

[The non-dual dharma-gate] non-dual means no duality. The real aspect of all dharmas, all things equally as they truly are, without distinction between one and another, is called non-dual. When a bodhisattva awakens to this principle that all is one, real and equal, it is called the “non-dual dharma-gate.” (For the real aspect of all dharmas, see in detail
the Real Aspect of All Dharmas
article)

“At that time, the bodhisattva Mahāmati, having praised the Buddha in verse, announced his own name: My name is Mahāmati, who is versed in the Great Vehicle; now with the one hundred and eight meanings, I respectfully ask the most honored of the honored.”
At that time, the bodhisattva Mahāmati
having
praised the Buddha in verse
and finishing
then
announced his own name: My name is Mahāmati, who is versed in the Great Vehicle; now
with
the one hundred and eight meanings,
I reverently
seek instruction
from
the World-Honored One (the most honored of the honored).
Thus what the bodhisattva Mahāmati is about to ask is
the one hundred and eight meanings

, and below he asks in one breath more than a hundred questions, which in fact is to lead toward the exposition of the one hundred and eight meanings; and the World-Honored One’s series of replies finally also come down to expounding the one hundred and eight meanings.
[The most honored of the honored]
the Buddha is
the most honored
among
the honored

, and so the Buddha is called the “most honored of the honored.” [Now with the one hundred and eight meanings, I respectfully ask the most honored of the honored] the “one hundred and eight meanings” are the principles of the “one hundred and eight phrases.” The “one hundred and eight phrases” spoken of here are precisely what the World-Honored One speaks below, and what all Buddhas speak, namely the phrases: “non-arising phrase, arising phrase; eternal phrase, impermanent phrase.
and so on. They are actually one hundred and three phrases; the number one hundred and eight is chosen as a round figure.

The meaning of the ‘one hundred and eight phrases’ is: no marks — within all marks, abandoning all marks. The Tang translation says: ‘Mahāmati! The Buddhas teach the Dharma in order to purify the two kinds of obstacles, the obstructing delusion and the obstructing knowledge,
and thus lead beings to abide progressively
among the one hundred and eight markless dharmas
in
it.” “

[The two kinds of obstacles, the obstructing delusion and the obstructing knowledge] the obstructing delusion and the obstructing knowledge, also called the affliction-obstacle and the knowable-obstacle. [The two obstacles] the affliction-obstacle and the knowable-obstacle. The affliction-obstacle is also called the delusion-obstacle; it refers to afflictions such as greed, hatred, and delusion, which cause sentient beings to revolve through birth and death within the three realms, thereby obstructing the work of nirvāṇa, and so it is called the “affliction-obstacle.” The knowable-obstacle is also called the knowledge-obstacle; it refers to the ignorance and wrong views of sentient beings, which cover over the understanding of wisdom and make it not keen, thereby obstructing the work of bodhi, and so it is called the “knowable-obstacle.” [No marks] within all marks, abandoning all marks. The Diamond Sutra says:
“To abandon all marks, this is called being a Buddha.”
[Clinging to marks] the Diamond Sutra says:
“All that has marks is all false and vain.”
To cling to marks is to take the marks as real, and then to give rise to discrimination (reflective calculation).

Since the “one hundred and eight meanings” are: no marks — within all marks, abandoning all marks. Therefore all discriminations are negated (arising and non-arising, eternal and impermanent, and so on; every kind of discrimination is a mistake) and all should be abandoned. So, the true aim of Mahāmati’s inquiry is not that the World-Honored One should answer these questions one by one, but that the World-Honored One should thereby expound the “one hundred and eight meanings.” Below, although Mahāmati in one breath raises more than a hundred questions, asking everywhere about all dharmas of the world and beyond the world, the World-Honored One does not answer his questions one by one, but only says that all these are without self-nature, and even wittily retorts that he has not asked comprehensively enough; finally it comes down to expounding the “one hundred and eight phrases,” and this is the true point —
“I shall speak to you of the realm of self-realization.”

For the realm of self-realization is precisely to abandon marks, to be far from every kind of discrimination; and Mahāmati’s questions are all views of discrimination, all clinging to marks. The Diamond Sutra says:
To abandon all marks
, this is called being a Buddha.”
The Tang translation says:
“Mahāmati, the great bodhisattvas, relying on the sacred teachings, have no discrimination. Dwelling alone in quiet, they observe self-realization, not awakened by another,
abandon the views of discrimination
, and advance higher and higher, entering the stage of the Tathāgata. Practicing thus is called the course of self-certified noble wisdom.”

“The World-Understander, hearing the verse they spoke, observed all the assembly, and said to the Buddha’s children: You who are Buddha’s children, now you may all freely ask, and I shall speak for you the realm of self-realization.”
The World-Honored One (the World-Understander), having heard the verse spoken by the bodhisattva Mahāmati, observed the whole assembly
, and seeing that the time had matured
, said to
them
You
who
are
Buddha’s
children
, may all
freely at will
raise
your
questions, and I
shall
proclaim for you
the realm of the Tathāgata’s
self-realization.
The point is set forth:
the realm of the Tathāgata’s
self-realization
— this is the central topic of this sutra.

[World-Understander] one of the ten titles of the Buddha; because the Buddha understands all things in the world and beyond the world, he is called the “World-Understander.” [Buddha’s children] refers to those who, trusting in the Buddha’s teachings, take up his family enterprise, and seeking to become Buddhas so that the Buddha-seed is never cut off
— this is an epithet of honor for the bodhisattvas
It also refers to the Buddha’s disciples and Buddhist believers.
“At that time, the bodhisattva Mahāmati, relying on the Buddha’s permission, bowed his head at the Buddha’s feet, and with palms joined in reverence, asked in verse:
At that time, the bodhisattva Mahāmati, relying on the Buddha’s permission, bowed his head at the Buddha’s feet, and with palms joined in reverence, asked in verse:
[Permit] the “permit” in “relying on the Buddha’s permission” means to grant permission (to hear and then to grant).
How is thought purified? How does thought increase? How is delusion seen? How does delusion increase?”
How
is
the false
thought
purified? Why
do
false thoughts instead increase
How
are
stupidity and confusion
clearly seen?
Why would
stupidity and confusion instead
increase
[How (yún hé)] in what way, why, how, and in what manner.
“Why do Buddha-lands transform, with marks and with all the heterodox teachers? How is the state of no-reception reached? Why is it called no-reception?
Why do
Buddha-lands
manifest forth all kinds of marks, and all
kinds
of heterodox teachers? How is the stage of no-reception reached? For what reason is it called no-reception?

[Heterodox teachers] those who establish a path outside Buddhism are called heterodox teachers, that is, the wrong teachings outside the truth. [No-reception] not receiving further existence (having done with birth and death, no longer receiving a body in a future life).
Why is it called Buddha’s child? To what place does liberation reach? Who is bound and who is freed?”
For what reason is it called Buddha’s child? When one cultivates the path and attains liberation, to what place will one go? Who is bound? Who is liberated?
What is the realm of meditative concentration? Why are there three vehicles? I beg that you explain.”
What is the state of meditative concentration like? Why are there three vehicles? I beg the World-Honored One to explain this for us.

[The three vehicles] the Śrāvaka vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, and the Bodhisattva vehicle. The Śrāvaka vehicle is also called the lesser vehicle, the Pratyekabuddha vehicle is also called the middle vehicle, and the Bodhisattva vehicle is also called the great vehicle.
“From what does dependent origination arise? How does the creator and the created come about? How is the explanation of both-and-different stated? How does it increase?”

All dharmas arise by dependent origination — so from what does this dependent origination itself arise? Since all dharmas arise from causes and conditions, why is there still a creator and a created? Why is it said “both exist and do not exist, neither exist nor not exist” (the explanation of both-and-different)? And why does it again go on increasing into all sorts of doctrines?

[The explanation of both-and-different] when describing the existence of things, there are four basic statements: it exists, it does not exist, both exist and do not exist, neither exists nor does not exist. Among these, “both exist and do not exist” is the “both,” and “neither exists nor does not exist” is the “different.”
the explanation of both-and-different
refers to “both exist and do not exist, neither exists nor does not exist.”
“What is the formless concentration
And the attainment of cessation? What is the cessation of thought? For what cause does one awaken from concentration?”
What is
the formless concentration (the four emptiness concentrations)
? What is

the attainment of cessation (the concentration of extinction)? What is the thoughtless concentration (the cessation of thought)? Since it is the thoughtless concentration (the cessation of thought), how is it that the thought of awareness rises again from within this concentration
then

[The four emptiness concentrations] this is the highest concentration of ordinary beings; after the body ends, one may be reborn in the four heavens of the formless realm, but one still cannot leave the three realms. [The concentration of extinction] this is a concentration of the world-transcending path, able to cut off delusion and be done with birth and death, and to escape the round of rebirth. [The thoughtless concentration] this is the meditation that the heterodox teachers cultivate in order to obtain the reward of the heaven of no-thought
a kind of meditation that extinguishes all thought whatsoever
of

the mind. After the body ends, one may be reborn in the heaven of no-thought, with a life span of five hundred kalpas; and when that life span is nearly spent, within the concentration the thought of awareness arises again, and one falls back into the round of rebirth. So although the thoughtless concentration can, within the concentration, keep thought from arising — like a fish in ice or a dormant insect — it cannot cut off delusion and attain the world-transcending noble fruit.
“How does the created arise, the entering forth and the holding of the body? How are discriminations manifested? How do the stages arise?”

Why do the bodhisattvas enter the world to save beings? How do they enter the world, and how do they still remain pure amid the defiled world? How do they manifest the body of discrimination? How do they awaken into the stages?

[The stages] refers to the ten stages. In the fifty-two stages of the bodhisattva’s practice, the fifth group of ten is called the ten stages. In these ten stages one gradually opens the Buddha-realm and accomplishes the wisdom of all species, and this already belongs to the noble stage, so it is also called the “ten noble ones.”
“Who breaks through the three existences? In what place and as what body? To what place does one go at rebirth?”
Who can
break through the three existences?
In what place
does one receive a body
At rebirth
to what place
does one go?

[The three existences] the birth and death of the three realms have a cause and an effect, and so they are called the “three existences.” First, the existence of desire, that is, the birth and death of the realm of desire; second, the existence of form, that is, the birth and death of the realm of form; third, the existence of formlessness, that is, the birth and death of the formless realm.
“Who are the most excellent children
and by what cause do they obtain spiritual powers and the self-mastering samādhi? What is the samādhi mind? O most excellent one, speak to me.”
Why are the great bodhisattvas able
to obtain spiritual powers and the self-mastering samādhi?
What is
the samādhi mind?
I beg the World-Honored One
to speak for me.
[The most excellent children]
the Buddha is
the most excellent
one, and his
children (
the great bodhisattvas
are called the most excellent children.
“What is called the storehouse? What are the mind and the consciousness?
What is the alaya-consciousness (the storehouse)? What is the manas (the mind) and the six consciousnesses (consciousness)?
How do arising and ceasing come about? How does right seeing return?
Why do the various views of arising and ceasing arise? How does one cut off the various views of arising and ceasing?
The Tang translation says: “How do the various views arise? How does one withdraw the various views?”
What are the lineages, the non-lineages, and the mind-measure?

Why is it said that the Śrāvaka, the Pratyekabuddha and the bodhisattva are the lineages that study Buddhism, while the heterodox teachers and the icchantikas are the non-lineages; and what is the measure of mind of each of them?
[Icchantika] an abbreviation of icchantika, meaning one for whom it is extremely difficult to become a Buddha.
How is the mark established, and what is the meaning of non-self?
Why is there the mark of a self, and what is the meaning of non-self?
How are there no sentient beings? How is it spoken in worldly convention?
Why does the ultimate truth say there are no sentient beings? And why does the conventional truth say there are sentient beings?

[The two truths] the ultimate truth and the conventional truth. The ultimate truth, also called the truth of highest meaning or the noble truth of supreme meaning, is the real principle seen by noble wisdom, that is, the content of dharma-nature inwardly realized, beyond words. The conventional truth, also called the worldly truth or the truth of mundane convention, is the worldly matters and marks that ordinary beings see.
What are the view of annihilation and the view of permanence, and how do they not arise?
What are the view of annihilation and the view of permanence, and how can one cause these two views not to arise?
How can the Buddha and the heterodox teachers have marks that do not contradict one another?”
Why is it said that the Buddha and the heterodox teachers, their marks do not contradict one another? (This is spoken with reference to the ultimate truth.)
How is it that in the future world there are all the various different schools?
Why, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, do the disciples again give rise to the various different views and establish the various schools?
Why is there emptiness and for what cause? Why is there moment-to-moment destruction?
Why are all dharmas empty in nature? And why do they again break down moment by moment?
How is the birth in the womb? Why is the world immovable?
What is it to be born through a womb? And why is it again said that the world is eternally immovable? (This is spoken with reference to the ultimate truth.)
For what cause are things like illusion, like a dream, like the city of the gandharvas, like the heat-haze of the world, and like the moon in water?
Why is the world like an illusion, like a dream, like the city of the gandharvas, like the heat-haze, and like the moon in water?

[The city of the gandharvas] that is, the city of the gandharvas, a metaphor for an illusion. The performers of the western regions are called gandharvas, and they conjure up by illusion a city, which vanishes in an instant; this is called a city of the gandharvas. And a mirage over the sea is also called a city of the gandharvas. [The heat-haze] also called the blaze of the sun, it is the vapor produced under the scorching sun; seen from afar it looks like water, a thirsty deer longs to drink and ultimately cannot, and this is used as a metaphor for an illusion.
Illusion, dream, the city of the gandharvas, the heat-haze, and the moon in water are five of the ten great-vehicle similes.

[The ten great-vehicle similes] the various great-vehicle scriptures often use ten similes — illusion, the heat-haze, the moon in water, empty space, an echo, the city of the gandharvas, a dream, a shadow, an image in a mirror, and a transformation — to set forth the principle of “emptiness.”
For what cause are the factors of enlightenment and the divisions of bodhi spoken of?
Why must one expound
the seven factors of enlightenment and the eightfold noble path
and
the thirty-seven divisions of bodhi
[The thirty-seven divisions of bodhi]
also called
the thirty-seven aids to enlightenment. The path is that which leads through; the provisions for the road to nirvāṇa,
in all
are thirty-seven
the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold noble path.
Why are the lands in chaos? How does the view of existence arise?”
Why are
the lands ruined and in chaos?
Since all dharmas are without essence, why does the view of existence arise?
How is there no arising and no ceasing, and the world is like a flower in the sky?”
Why is it said that the marks of the world
neither arise nor cease
, being like
a flower in the sky

[No arising and no ceasing] this term has two sharply opposed meanings. The “no arising and no ceasing” spoken by the heterodox teachers means an eternal existence. The “no arising and no ceasing” spoken in Buddhism means: all dharmas never existed at all (being originally never arisen, therefore also nothing to cease) — this is the real aspect of all dharmas (the actual state of all dharmas). The Buddha-treasury Sutra
, the
Chapter on Buddha-recitation, Part Two, says:
“What is called the real aspect of all dharmas? It is that all dharmas are ultimately empty, having nothing at all.”
The Perfect Enlightenment Sutra says:
“All sentient beings, within the unborn, falsely see arising and ceasing; therefore it is said they turn in the wheel of birth and death.”
The Sutra of the Most Excellent King says:
“The unborn is real; birth is false and vain. The foolish, drifting in birth and death; the Tathāgata is real in essence, without the false and vain, and this is called nirvāṇa.”
The Sutra of the Benevolent King says:
“All dharmas, in nature real and empty, coming not and going not, without arising and without ceasing, the same as true reality, equal to dharma-nature.”
How does one awaken within the world? Why is the abandoning of words spoken of?”
Why awaken within the world? And why speak of abandoning all marks?
Who is it that abandons false imagination? Why is the simile of empty space used?”
Who is it that abandons false imagination? And why is it said that, like empty space, one is equal and unmoving?
How many kinds of thusness are there? How many minds of pāramitā are there?”
How many kinds of thusness are there? And how many minds of pāramitā are there?
For what cause does one cross over the stages? Who reaches the state of no-reception?”
For what cause
does one go beyond the ten stages to the Buddha-stage,
and who reaches
the state of no-reception
the Buddha-realm
Which are the two non-selfs? How is the realm of wisdom (eryang) purified?”
How does one have no self of persons and no self of dharmas? And how does one purify the realm of wisdom (eryang)?
How many kinds of wisdom are there? How many kinds of precepts for the natures of sentient beings?”
How many kinds of right wisdom are there? And since sentient beings have different root-natures, how many kinds of precepts are there?
Who gives birth to the natures of the jewels, the mani-pearl and true pearls and the like?”
The mani-pearl, true pearls, and the other jewels
from
what
are they born
Who gives birth to the various languages and the various natures of sentient beings?”
Who causes sentient beings to have all the different languages and natures?
The clear fields and the arts — who is it that reveals them?”
The five fields of knowledge and the arts (skills and techniques) — who created and invented them?
[The five fields of knowledge] the five branches of learning of ancient India
the science of language (philology), the science of crafts (
technology
), the science of medicine, the science of logic, and the inner science (the study of religion)
How many kinds of gāthā are there, the long verse and the short verse?”
Recitation
the long verse and the short verse
— how many kinds of each are there
[Gāthā]
rendered into Chinese:
recitation
How many kinds of doctrine are there? What is called a treatise?”
How many kinds of doctrine are there
the Tang translation
says
How many different principles are there
? And why is it called a treatise?
[Treatise] to take the essential meaning spoken of in the scriptures, to distinguish and arrange it, or to explain it, is called a “treatise.”
How does food and drink arise, and how do the various cravings of desire arise?”
Why is there food and drink, and also the various cravings of desire?
What is called a king, the wheel-turning king and the lesser kings? How does one guard the country?”
